- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true high.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model delays response — adjust forecast downward early in the horizon.
- Model underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods — increase forecast spread or add 1–2% upward bias.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 85), model overestimates continuation — reduce forecast slope downward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak or trough.
- In absence of clear event context, model defaults to “flat” behavior — introduce 0.5–1% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
